title: Consider recording the "duplicate-attribute" error state.

labels.name: security/privacy
labels.description: There are security or privacy implications

body:
CSP attempts to defend against some kinds of dangling-markup attacks by [preventing the execution of scripts that include "`<script`" in an attribute name or value](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#is-element-nonceable). Discarding attributes during parsing makes it possible to trivially work around this defense, as described in <https://crbug.com/740615>. As dropping repeated attributes is also the root cause of the dangling-markup risk in the first place, it might be reasonable to dig into it a little more deeply to see if something more fundamental can be done.

One idea we (briefly) [discussed at TPAC](https://www.w3.org/2017/11/06-webappsec-minutes.html#item08) is to prevent nonced script execution for `<script>` elements which had [duplicate-attribute parse errors](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parse-error-duplicate-attribute). An approach to this that I'm exploring in https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/566822 does more or less the following:

1.  Records duplicate-attribute parse errors on the tag during tokenization.
2.  Persists that error bit onto the `Node` generated during tree-building.
3.  Reads that error bit during ["Is element nonceable?"](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#is-element-nonceable).

WDYT?

/cc @whatwg/security (@ckerschb, @dbates-wk, @patrickkettner in particular as folks working on CSP)
